projects.title: Oral History Analysis for “Freedom to Thrive” Exhibit
projects.description: Partnered with the Colorado Springs Pioneers Museum to conduct oral history research for the Freedom to Thrive exhibit, part of the U.S. Semiquincentennial and Colorado Sesquicentennial commemorations, as part of a Community-Based Research course (SO328). Analyzed interviews from historically marginalized communities and collaborated with the Curator of History to deliver an interpretive memo informing exhibit narrative and design.

projects.title: Neighborhood University Alumni Data Analysis
projects.description: Partnered with Hey Neighbor’s Neighborhood University program, as part of a Community-Based Praxis course (SO411), to analyze engagement across 200+ alumni in 50+ neighborhoods. Worked with the Executive Director to clean and structure datasets using Excel and Stata, and used ArcGIS to visualize community patterns, supporting program evaluation and future outreach strategy.

activity.title: Coral orange backgrounds are taking over LinkedIn this month, and that's because ColorStack just hosted the Stacked Up Summit! The first event of the weekend, the Alumni Welcome & Opening Keynote, set the tone for the entire summit. Was I an alumnus? Not quite, I've still got one year of improv comedy left at Colorado College . But Ethan Reece offered me a seat at his table anyway, where we ended up chatting about college sports until the keynote began. That's when Kay Malcolm urged us to show up big and be our unique selves, and Jeffrey Malcolm pushed us to be confident in who we are. Other memorable moments included the fireside chat, where Dr. Miguel Angel Hernandez challenged us to reframe cultural lessons in ways that don't hold us back, and Keiyana Arnold, MSOM spoke on building a personal brand through authentic relationships. There was also a panel with ColorStack alumni, where Marcelo Chaman Mallqui talked about his journey being delusionally ambitious and leading design at Gumloop . Yet, my favorite moment came during closing remarks from Jehron W. Petty and Rami Abdou , who shared the story of ColorStack by giggling and finishing each other's sentences. Frankly, that's the real friendship and connection that happens here in this community. Their journey building ColorStack, and more recently transitioning into the tech industry, Jehron now at TextQL and Rami at Netflix , was genuinely powerful to hear, and as they opened up, they left us with a reminder to stay methodical in our processes. To everyone I met, sat with, learned from, and danced with this weekend, thank you for making this summit one to remember, coral orange background and all! ...more

Some Thursdays you just bike downtown, leading a group of friends with Audrey Pozen , to see an exhibit you helped curate finally open to the public. Today was one of those days! "Freedom to Thrive: The American Experiment in Colorado Springs" just opened at the Colorado Springs Pioneers Museum , and getting to contribute to it through my Community Based Research course in the Sociology Department at Colorado College was one of my favorite parts of this past school year. In January, we spent weeks transcribing oral histories and drafting a thematic memo based on these lived experiences. This exhibit draws on stories from individuals in historic communities with deep roots in Colorado Springs. It includes anecdotes of how barriers to integration made abandoning one's culture feel more attainable than fighting to preserve it. It's powerful, it's honest, and it's beautifully done. To Leah Davis Witherow , thank you for doing the work that sparks conversations we need but so often shy away from, for taking these stories of integration, culture, and resistance, and giving them the light they deserve. If you're in the Springs, go bike over and see it, and bring friends too! Free admission, 215 South Tejon Street. ...more

If anyone knows any good ol' bagel shops near Berkeley, let me know. After a long night debugging at Cal Hacks UC Berkeley AI Hackathon over the past weekend, Ava Gonick , John Connell , Eric Fu and I were searching for one the next morning. Our project, Retention, won 3rd Place for Best Use of TokenRouter. We built an AI system that uses an fMRI-based prediction model to estimate viewer engagement across educational videos, identify the moments where students are most likely to lose focus, and run a two-agent editing loop that revises those segments until predicted retention improves. Always fun tinkering with AI at the intersection of learning, neuroscience, and human behavior! A huge thank you to Christine Dai from PaleBlueDot AI for sponsoring and supporting our project. Really enjoyed the debugging marathon with Ava, John, and Eric and the continued pursuit for bagels! ...more

Any time I said I was taking “Generative Art” this past month people often assumed AI and I would have to explain it wasn’t that simple. This class deepened how I think about art with algorithms, from something focused on prompt-based outputs to something grounded in systems, process, and creative exploration. That perspective has carried into my weaving practice, where I explored repetition, rhythm, and simple rules as ways to build experimental patterns like Jacquard loom textiles. For our class projections, my team worked with cables.gl and Shadertoy to build a system of geometric and fractal-like patterns inspired by the architecture of Charles L. Tutt Library. Explore the project here: https://cables.gl/p/n3siud Really grateful for a computer science elective that let code, creativity, and art actually meet in practice! ...more

More than 20 Colorado College students came together to create Tiger HaCCs 1.0, CC's first annual 24-hour hackathon. They worked through the night to design tech solutions focused on community revitalization. Partnering with the City of Colorado Springs , student teams from eight different majors collaborated on real-world challenges, including civic engagement and volunteer access. The winning project was a gamified platform connecting volunteers with local nonprofits. “This event came naturally to students, thanks to the Block Plan’s condensed schedule, which encourages deep learning, focus, and exploration,” says Marcos Arnold ’27. Read more about the event in the comments below. ...more ...more

I spearheaded Colorado College 's first interdisciplinary hackathon in partnership with the City of Colorado Springs . Over the past few months, I helped bring Tiger HaCCs 1.0 to life — designing polished graphics that showcased Colorado’s natural beauty, building a responsive static website, mentoring innovative teams, and supporting creative presentations and impactful projects throughout the weekend. We had 20+ participants from 8+ majors, a true liberal arts collaboration tackling real civic challenges. At one point, I even had to explain to Campus Safety at 4am that the people still in the building were just students fully immersed in their projects, prototyping solutions for our Community Revitalization theme. Incredibly grateful to our judges — Lilly Chen , Lizzie Blaschke , Shakanah Tedder , Robin Lovewell, CWDP , Celeste Diaz Ferraro , Jon-Michael Horst , and Coral Laski — from FSH Technologies , Exponential Impact , and the City of Colorado Springs for lending their time, constructive feedback, and enthusiastic support this weekend. A huge thank you to Emma Fairburn , Varsha Koushik , Izzy Wagenvoord , and my rockstar Coding Club leadership team buddies— Ronan Takizawa , Maddy Spark , and Parthib Paul — for helping bring this vision to life. We really made it happen! Proud of what we accomplished and looking forward to Tiger HaCCs 2.0 — more projects, more collaboration, and hopefully fewer late-night surprise visits from Campus Safety! ...more

Yooo LinkedIn Family!! we've got news. 🥳 I'm joining Todd as their Software Engineer Intern for the Fall! And I'm not walking in alone. Jose Cruz-Lopez , my brother from the ColorStack community, is joining too. Same startup. Same program. A year ago we were two first-gen kids hyping each other up through the slack huddles and threads pulling generational numbers as a duo. Now we share a team. If you don't know Todd : they're a frontier research lab out of LA building foundation technology and crop genetics for sustainable agriculture. Their mission is literally to make sustainable agriculture benefit all of humanity. Here's why that hits different for me. I spent two years at SNHU researching food insecurity, how kids in New England actually get fed when the school day ends. That work changed how I see technology: it's only as valuable as the problems it solves for real people. So writing software for a team reimagining how food gets grown? That's not random. That's alignment. 😤✌️ From researching the food system to engineering for it. From meeting through ColorStack to building at the same startup. None of this happens without community and the people who believed first. Community isn't just support, it's a pipeline. Find your people. Pour into them. One day you're building the future next to them. That's the whole playbook. ✌️

This weekend, I had the honor of showing up powerfully for the virtual component of the 2026 HSF STEM Summit. Having previously attended the HSF National Leadership Conference, I came in knowing how strong the HSF Scholar network was, and I’m excited to be a part of a STEM-centered community now. During this conference, I connected with and learned from HSF staff, mentors, and fellow Latino professionals in STEM fields. Through sessions on Well-Being, Financial Wellness, Tools for Career Success in the Age of AI, and Conversations with Leaders, I gained valuable insights and preparation for the in-person component in Los Angeles, CA. I am incredibly grateful to HSF for selecting me for this opportunity and for continuing to provide scholars with these opportunities. I would also like to give a special thank you to my Supergroup 5 (The High Fives 👏) program lead, Leticia Barreto- Castillo, MBA , and my Group 9 mentors, Paloma St.Clair and Jose Casillas Zubiria , for their guidance, encouragement, and mentorship throughout the virtual component. I also want to express my gratitude to my peers in Mentor Group 9, Supergroup 5, and every scholar I had the opportunity to meet, learn from, and grow alongside. Last but certainly not least, thank you to this year’s STEM Summit sponsors, Honda and ABM Industries , for making this event possible. #HSF #HSFSCHOLAR #STEM26

I’m so grateful to see Freedom to Thrive: The American Experiment in Colorado Springs open its doors after so much thoughtful collaboration. I only wish I could be there to experience it in person! It’s incredibly rewarding to watch this work come to fruition and know that I had the opportunity to contribute to a project that amplifies the voices and histories of our Colorado Springs community. Congratulations to everyone who made this possible, and especially to our community curators and Leah Davis Witherow for her vision and dedication. It's an honor to have played a small part in work that invites such important conversations. If you're in Colorado Springs, be sure to check it out!

honors_and_awards.description: Received funding to pursue an independent research project titled "Rhythms of Resistance: Music, Identity, and Activism in the Caribbean." This project explored how music traditions such as bomba, plena, and palos have historically served as forms of resistance in Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic.
